primitives.name: Spatio-Contextual Perceiver Resampler
primitives.verbatim_quote: To address these challenges, we propose Spatio-Contextual Perceiver Resampler (SCPR), a framework for single-anchored dense soccer video captioning.
primitives.assumptions: Video segments are temporally ordered; player positions are accurately tracked; global context enhances local captioning fidelity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When local features lack sufficient temporal or spatial discriminability.

layer2.mapping: SCPR's global-local integration mirrors GSI's multi-scale belief propagation across video frames and player states.
layer2.telemetry: CIDEr score improvement and spotting-stage F1 increase.

primitives.name: Global-Local Feature Integration
primitives.verbatim_quote: SCPR combines three components: (1) global-local feature integration for incorporating long-range video context around each caption anchor; (2) spatial position encoding based on the absolute 2D locations of players; and (3) cross-modal feature fusion that aligns global, local, and spatial features with a trainable language decoder.
primitives.assumptions: Long-range context improves caption accuracy; temporal coherence exists between adjacent video segments.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When short-term local features fail to capture game dynamics.

layer2.mapping: Enables GSE to reason over extended game sequences by embedding global context into local caption anchors.
layer2.telemetry: Improved recall and F1 in event-spotting tasks.

primitives.name: Spatial Position Encoding
primitives.verbatim_quote: SCPR combines three components: (1) global-local feature integration for incorporating long-range video context around each caption anchor; (2) spatial position encoding based on the absolute 2D locations of players; and (3) cross-modal feature fusion that aligns global, local, and spatial features with a trainable language decoder.
primitives.assumptions: Player positions are deterministic within frame boundaries; spatial layout correlates with game events.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When positional ambiguity leads to incorrect event interpretation.

layer2.mapping: Maps player coordinates to semantic roles in GSE's state transition graph.
layer2.telemetry: Enhanced caption detail and event-sequence consistency.

reasoning_traces.think:
SCPR addresses limitations in existing dense captioning by integrating global temporal context and explicit player positions. It employs a perceiver-based resampling mechanism to combine global and local features, enabling richer spatial and sequential detail in generated captions. The framework uses a large language model as a decoder, aligning multimodal inputs—video features, spatial positions, and global context—with textual output. This approach mitigates the dilution of critical event cues caused by abundant irrelevant visual information. The method's dual nature allows it to maintain both local specificity and global coherence, enhancing narrative richness. However, strict localization precision remains a challenge, indicating potential trade-offs between descriptive depth and temporal accuracy. The framework’s design reflects a synthesis of computer vision and NLP, leveraging cross-modal alignment for improved sports understanding.
